name: sensitive-data-insights
title: Sensitive Data Insights (Security-Focused Analytics)
description: Architecture blueprint for analytics on sensitive/regulated data: land data in a Lakehouse, apply access controls (OneLake data-access roles, sensitivity labels, workspace RBAC), mask/aggregate in transforms, and serve only governed outputs to BI. Best when strict access control and data protection are first-class requirements.
best_for: Regulated or sensitive data (PII, financial, health) where access control, masking, and sensitivity labeling matter as much as the analytics itself.
primary_storage: Lakehouse (raw/masked layers) + optional Warehouse (aggregated, broadly shareable)
key_ingestion: Copy Job / Dataflow / Pipeline (ideally over private/managed connectivity)

item_set.purpose: Aggregated, de-identified data safe to share more broadly
Ingest sensitive source data (prefer private connectivity)

governance_controls.purpose: Restrict which principals can read which lakehouse folders/tables (fine-grained data access).
Classify/label items (and enforce downstream protection) — apply/list via the label group.
Least-privilege workspace roles; separate raw vs curated workspaces for isolation.
Reach sensitive sources over managed private endpoints instead of public network.

decisions.guidance: Keep raw sensitive data isolated in the lakehouse with tight OneLake roles; publish only aggregated/de-identified data to a Warehouse for broader consumption.
Defense in depth: OneLake roles at the data layer, labels for classification/DLP, RLS at the BI layer. Layer them; do not rely on one.
For sensitive sources prefer managed private endpoints / private connectivity over public network paths.

build_with.deploy_ordering: Lakehouse/Warehouse (Foundation) before transforms and reports; apply OneLake roles + labels + workspace RBAC after items exist. fabio deploy handles item ordering; governance controls are applied as a follow-up.
outline: Create an isolated lakehouse (and optional aggregated warehouse); consider a dedicated workspace.
Restrict access: OneLake data-access roles (onelake-security), sensitivity labels (label), least-privilege workspace roles.
Ingest over private connectivity (managed-private-endpoint) where possible.
Mask/tokenize/aggregate in notebooks; write only de-identified outputs to the shareable layer.
Model with RLS + report only on approved, governed data.
